_about: What a filer needs for each of the 50 states and the District of Columbia: the office that receives a special education due process complaint, its official filing page, and how to reach it. Compiled from official state pages in August and September 2026 (the research behind Sped DPC) and trimmed to what a filer uses. Start from filingUrl, the state’s official page on filing a due process complaint, and confirm every value there before relying on it: pages, forms and addresses change. Contacts are offices, not people; where a state sends filings to a named staff member, the current contact is on filingUrl. filingEmail and filingFax are the office’s; acceptsEmail and acceptsFax say whether the official pages say a complaint may be filed that way (null: not stated). limitationsMonths is the state’s own window where the research found one; null means none was found, so the federal two years of 34 C.F.R. § 300.507(a)(2) applies unless the state’s page says otherwise. alsoServeDistrict: a copy goes to the school district as well. pageChecked records whether filingUrl opened when last checked.

states.name: Alaska
states.filingOffice: Special Education Dispute Resolution, Alaska Department of Education & Early Development
states.filingAddress:
Special Education Dispute Resolution
P.O. Box 110500
Juneau, Alaska 99811-0500
states.filingNote: Give written notice of the request to the school district and send a copy to Special Education Dispute Resolution at the Alaska Department of Education & Early Development by mail, fax ((907) 465-2806), or email (sped@alaska.gov). The state's model form is optional. A parent must request a hearing within 12 months after the date the school district provides written notice of the decision the parent disagrees with.

Special Education Services

P.O. Box 30201
Montgomery, AL 36130
states.filingNote: File with the Alabama State Department of Education by mail (SES DPH, P.O. Box 30201, Montgomery) or by email to dph@alsde.edu. At the same time, send a copy to the superintendent of the school district or public agency serving the child; the sample form is optional. The complaint must concern a violation that occurred not more than two years before the parent or agency knew or should have known about it.

Little Rock, Arkansas 72201
states.filingNote: Give the written request to the school district and forward a copy to the Director, Office of Special Education, Arkansas Department of Education; official sources give different mailing addresses, and email or fax filing is not stated on the official pages researched. The complaint must concern a violation that occurred not more than two years before the parent or agency knew or should have known about it. Confirm on the official filing page.

states.filingNote: Give the complaint to the school district or charter school and forward a copy to the Arizona Department of Education's Dispute Resolution Unit through its online portal, by email to ESSDRInbox@azed.gov, by fax to 602-364-0641, or by mail to 1535 West Jefferson Street, where the state's own documents give two different mail stops (Bin #62 and Bin #24). The model form is optional, and the complaint must concern a violation not more than two years before the filing party knew or should have known about it. Confirm on the official filing page.

states.filingNote: Serve the school district first: the Office of Administrative Hearings accepts a document only after it has been served on the other parties, and a proof of service must go to OAH with the complaint. File with OAH's Special Education Division by mail, hand delivery, or overnight delivery; OAH does not accept email or fax, and its Secure e-File Transfer system requires a signed SE-CESA agreement on file first and does not serve the other parties. Confirm on the official filing page.

The form is optional, the alleged violations must have occurred no more than two years before the complaint is filed, and CDE publishes two different mailing addresses for this office. Confirm on the official filing page.

states.filingNote: Send the Request for Impartial Special Education Hearing form to the Connecticut State Department of Education's Due Process Unit and to the school district. The form lists an email (dueprocess.sde@ct.gov) and fax (860-713-7153) for the unit, but whether they are accepted for filing is not stated on the official pages researched. A party has two years to request a hearing from the time the board of education proposed or refused to initiate or change the child's identification, evaluation, placement, or provision of a free appropriate public education.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.filingOffice: Office of the State Superintendent of Education, Office of Dispute Resolution
states.filingAddress:
Office of Dispute Resolution
1050 First Street, NE, 3rd Floor, Washington, DC 20002
states.filingNote: Give the complaint to the local education agency you are complaining against (where DCPS is that agency, the form directs notice by e-fax to (202) 442-5115) and deliver a copy to OSSE's Office of Dispute Resolution the same day. ODR takes its copy by hand at 1050 First Street, NE, 3rd Floor, by fax to (202) 478-2956, or by email to Hearing.Office@dc.gov; a late copy may delay assignment of the hearing officer. A hearing must be requested within two (2) years of the date the parent or agency knew or should have known about the issue.

Electronic signatures are acceptable. The complaint must allege a violation that occurred not more than 2 years before the parent or agency knew or should have known about it.

The request must allege a violation not more than two (2) years before the parent or agency knew or should have known about it. The state's forms give two emails (BEESScomplaints@fldoe.org and, on the newer form, DueProcess@fldoe.org) and no fax number, so confirm on the official filing page.

Atlanta, Georgia 30334
states.filingNote: Send the request to the school district's superintendent and to the Georgia Department of Education at the same time. GaDOE accepts it by U.S. mail, eFax (770-344-4458), or email (spedhelpdesk@doe.k12.ga.us), strongly encourages electronic submission, and does not require its form. The request must allege a violation that occurred not more than two years before the parent or district knew or should have known about it.

Honolulu, HI 96804
states.filingNote: Hawaii has one statewide school district: submit the request (Form 105) to the Complex Area Superintendent, the Department of Education's Complaints Management Program (specialedcomplaints@k12.hi.us), and the Attorney General's Office of Dispute Resolution (atg.odr@hawaii.gov). The form prints no mailing address, and whether a mailed request to P.O. Box 2360 is accepted is not stated on the official pages researched. The request must allege a violation not more than two years before the parent or department knew or should have known about it; a separate state time limit (HRS §302A-443) applies to reimbursement claims for a unilateral placement.

states.filingNote: Send the signed complaint (the model form or any written statement with the required content) to the school district, area education agency, or other public agency involved and to the Iowa Department of Education, by email to ideadisputeresolution@iowa.gov or by mail to the Grimes State Office Building, 400 E. 14th St., Des Moines. An administrative law judge appointed by the Department conducts the hearing. The complaint must allege a violation that occurred not more than two years before the parent or agency knew or should have known about it.

Also give a copy to the special education director of the district or charter school named and check the box on the form confirming it; fax filing is not stated on the official pages researched. A due process complaint must be filed within two (2) years of the date the parent knew or should have known about the alleged violation.

The superintendent forwards it to the State Board within 5 days, as ISBE's parent form (ISBE 19-86A) also says. The request must be filed no more than 2 years after the date the parent or school district knew or should have known of the events it is based on.

states.filingNote: File with the Office of Administrative Law Proceedings, preferably through the I-CHAMP portal (https://ichamp.doe.in.gov), or by mail, fax (317-232-0261), or in-person delivery, and send the request to the school district's or charter school's superintendent at the same time; OALP does not accept filings by email. The current form (Revised June 2025) must be printed and signed by hand, since unsigned requests are not processed, and the older Department of Education form is superseded. A hearing must be requested within two years of the date the parent or school knew or should have known about the issue.

Topeka, Kansas 66612
states.filingNote: Send the signed notice to both the district superintendent or special education director (at the district's business office) and KSDE Special Education and Title Services Dispute Resolution; the hearing is held at the local level, and the sample form is optional. The problem must have occurred not more than two years before the complaint is filed, and email or fax filing is not stated on the official pages researched. The form gives Suite 620 while KSDE's general address is Suite 102, so confirm on the official filing page.

The state gives a three-year window: the violation must have happened not more than three years before the parent or district knew or should have known about it. Confirm on the official filing page.

La. R.S. 17:1946 now allows two years from when the parent knew or should have known, but the state's own page and form still say one year, and they give different mailing addresses (P.O. Box 94064 and 1201 North 3rd Street). Confirm on the official filing page.

states.filingNote: File the request with the Bureau of Special Education Appeals (the hearing office, not the state education agency) and send it to the school district at the same time, confirming in writing that the district was sent it and how. The BSEA accepts filings by mail or in person at 14 Summer Street, 4th Floor, Malden, by fax to (781) 397-4770, or by email to bseapleadings@mass.gov; its hearing request form is optional and may be completed in the home language. A hearing must be requested within two years of when the parent knew or should have known about the events the complaint is based on.

Office of Administrative Hearings

OAH accepts due process complaints by mail or hand delivery to 11101 Gilroy Road, Hunt Valley, or by fax to 410-229-4277, and does not accept them by email. The hearing must be requested within two years of the date the parent or agency knew about the alleged action.

At the same time, send a copy to the school district Superintendent and sign the form's certification that you did; an expedited request uses its own form, sent to the same office. The request must allege a violation that occurred not more than two years before the parent or school knew or should have known about it.

states.filingNote: File the signed complaint with the Michigan Department of Education, Office of Special Education – Due Process Complaints, by mail, hand delivery, fax (517-241-7141), or email (MDE-MIComplaints@michigan.gov), and give a copy to the school district or other public agency named. The department refers it to the Michigan Office of Administrative Hearings and Rules, which appoints the administrative law judge. A complaint must be filed within two years of the date the parent or district knew or should have known about the issues.

states.filingNote: Give the request to the school district and send a copy to the Minnesota Department of Education's Due Process Hearing Coordinator, noting on the form the date the district was sent its copy; MDE forwards it to the Court of Administrative Hearings. The form names mail and email (mde.dispute-resolution@state.mn.us) as filing methods, fax filing is not stated on the official pages researched, and this is separate from Minnesota's state complaint process. A complaint must be filed within two years of the date the parent or district knew or should have known about the alleged action.

Box 480, Jefferson City), fax (573-751-3910, Attention: Compliance Section), or email (secompliance@dese.mo.gov), and send a copy to the school district. Use the fax and email printed on the form, not the general office contacts on the department's webpage; DESE refers the request to the Administrative Hearing Commission. A hearing must be requested within two years of the date the parent or district knew or should have known about the issue.

Box), or fax it to (601) 359-1829, and send a copy to the school district; email filing is not stated on the official pages researched. The form's instructions borrow wording from the state complaint process, so check the required contents against the state's Procedural Safeguards notice. A hearing must be requested within two (2) years of the date the parent or agency knew or should have known about the issue.

Dispute Resolution Office

states.filingNote: Send the request to the Dispute Resolution Office, Superintendent of Public Instruction, P.O. Box 202501, Helena, by mail or hand delivery only; the Office of Public Instruction does not accept faxed or electronically transmitted requests. Also mail a copy to the school district and certify that on the form, which is voluntary. The complaint must allege a violation that happened not more than two years before the parent or district knew or should have known about it.

Office of Administrative Hearings
1711 New Hope Church Road

states.filingNote: File the petition (Form H-06E, or Form H-06E-A for a manifestation determination) with the Office of Administrative Hearings by mail, hand delivery, fax to (984) 236-1871 during business hours, or email to oah.clerks@oah.nc.gov with the petition attached as a PDF or Word file. Also mail or deliver a copy to the superintendent of the board of education named, recording it on the Certificate of Service, and mail or fax a copy to the N.C. Department of Public Instruction (6356 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-6356; fax (919) 807-3243). North Carolina's window is one year: the violation must have occurred not more than one year before the party knew or reasonably should have known about it.

states.filingNote: Send the due process complaint to both the school district and the North Dakota Department of Public Instruction's Office of Specially Designed Services, by mail, email (dpispecialed@nd.gov), or fax ((701) 328-4149). State form SFN 9461 is optional, and whether its online submit button counts as filing is not stated on the official pages researched. The complaint must allege a violation that occurred no more than two years before the parent or agency knew or should have known about it.

The rule's address (State Office Building, 6th Floor, 301 Centennial Mall South) is no longer where the Department is, and its contact page gives P.O. Box 94987 for mail and 500 S. 84th St. as its physical address, so confirm on the official filing page. The petition must be filed within two (2) years of the date the parent or agency knew or should have known about the alleged action.

NH Department of Education

Concord, NH 03301
states.filingNote: Send the original written request to the school district and a copy to the New Hampshire Department of Education's Governance Unit, Dispute Resolution and Constituent Complaints Section, 25 Hall Street, Concord, and keep a copy. Email and fax filing are not stated on the official pages researched, and the state's model form is not currently linked. The request must be made within 2 years of when the violation was or reasonably should have been discovered, but a claim for the costs of a unilateral special education placement must be brought within 90 days of the placement.

Box 500, Trenton, and send one copy of the entire request to the school district responsible for the child. Do not send exhibits to the Office of Special Education; fax filing for these requests is not stated on the official pages researched. A request must be filed within two years of the date the party knew or should have known about the alleged action.

Director of Special Education

New Mexico Public Education Department

Santa Fe, NM 87501
states.filingNote: File with the New Mexico Public Education Department through its online dispute-resolution system, by email to dispute.resolution@ped.nm.gov, or by mail to the Director of Special Education, c/o Office of General Counsel, 300 Don Gaspar Ave, Santa Fe; the model form is optional. PED's older 2020 safeguards notice also says to send the request to the district superintendent, which the current pages do not address, and fax filing is not stated on the official pages researched. The request must allege a violation that happened not more than two years before the parent or district knew or should have known about it.

states.name: Nevada
states.filingOffice: Nevada Department of Education, Superintendent of Public Instruction
states.filingNote: File the complaint with the head of the public agency (the district superintendent or the charter authority) and, at the same time, forward a copy to the Superintendent of Public Instruction at the Nevada Department of Education; Nevada has no state filing address. How the state copy should be delivered is not stated on the official pages researched, and disputeresolution@doe.nv.gov is published as a contact, not a filing channel. The complaint must be filed within 2 years after the parent or agency knew or should have known about the alleged action.

Office of Special Education

The district appoints the hearing officer (New York City uses its own impartial hearing system), and email or fax filing is not stated on the official pages researched. A hearing must be requested within two years of the date the parent or district knew or should have known about the issue.

Ohio Department of Education and Workforce

Due process timelines do not begin until the district receives the request, and the 2025 form does not mention fax. The complaint must allege a violation that occurred not more than two years before the parent or agency knew or should have known about it.

Fax filing is not stated on the official pages researched, and the state form is optional as long as the complaint contains the required elements. The complaint must allege a violation that happened not more than two years before the parent or district knew or should have known about it.

The request counts as filed on the date ODE receives it, and it is filed with ODE, not the Office of Administrative Hearings. The state's safeguards notice gives two years from when the parent or district knew or should have known, but the state rule as quoted in a hearing order counts two years from the act or omission, so confirm on the official filing page.

The form is optional, and fax filing is not stated on the official pages researched. Pennsylvania has no explicit state time frame, and its procedural safeguards notice says to request a hearing within two years of the date the parent or district knew or should have known about the issue.
